basic_identification.full_title: Packaging — Complete, Filled Transport Packages — Stability Testing of Unit Loads
basic_identification.sector_category: Transport Engineering / Transport Packages and Packaging Codes (approved by the Transport Engineering Division Council and finalized by the Transport Packages and Packaging Codes Sectional Committee of the Bureau of Indian Standards)

sectional_committee.name: Transport Packages and Packaging Codes Sectional Committee

scope.summary: This standard specifies methods of testing for the stability of completely formed, filled unit loads. These tests are designed to assess the performance of unit loads when subjected to the mechanical and environmental hazards of land-based handling, storage, and transportation (including pallet, clamp, and push/pull handling).

certification_and_marking.standard_type: Performance and Testing Standard (Transport Engineering / Package Testing)
certification_and_marking.certification_status: Voluntary Quality and Performance Testing Standard. Under BIS Scheme I, certification is on a voluntary basis. However, compliance with IS 15526 is widely mandated inside corporate logistics contracts, Indian Navy and defense supply-chain packaging specifications, FMCG warehousing tenders, and commercial logistics/shipping audits to certify that palletized and clamped unit loads remain stable on road-going trucks and warehouse storage racks to prevent damage. Precious metal hallmarking is completely inapplicable.

requirements.detail: The test package shall normally be filled with its intended contents. However, simulated or dummy contents may be used on condition that the dimensions and physical properties of such contents shall be as close as possible to those of the intended contents.
Ensure that the test package is closed normally, as if ready for distribution. If simulated or dummy contents are used, ensure that the normal method of closure is still employed.
Prior to testing, prepared unit loads must be conditioned in a standardized atmosphere according to IS 7031 to reach moisture equilibrium.

Simulates the dynamic forces of forklift and pallet-truck handling. Focuses on evaluating the physical displacement, shifting, or structural damage of the unit load during lifting, maneuvering, and stacking.

Evaluates the compression resistance of unit loads when compressed from opposite sides by clamp truck attachments. Verifies that packages do not collapse, buckle, or shift under calculated squeeze forces.
Evaluates the stability of unit loads utilizing slip sheets. Simulates the dynamic force of a forklift's push/pull attachment grabbing, pulling, and pushing the slip sheet onto a load plate.

requirements.requirement_type: Annex A Lift Truck Handling Tests
requirements.detail: Details a series of lift truck handling tests including flat push, over-tilting, acceleration/deceleration, and obstacle course testing in accordance with ASTM D6055 or ISO 10531 guidelines to simulate warehouse handling.

With one edge of the unit load supported by a hard, solid surface (for example, concrete), raise the other end of the load until the base is 20 cm above the floor level and release it to fall freely. This must be repeated for specified edge combinations to evaluate impact resistance.

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 15526 : 2004 is the national Indian Standard code of practice specifying methods for testing the stability of complete, filled transport unit loads. Based on the international standard ISO 10531:1992, it provides a comprehensive testing framework to evaluate how palletized, clamped, or slip-sheeted cargo assemblies withstand the physical and dynamic hazards of warehouse handling, mechanical stacking, and land-based transport. It regulates package preparation (using real or closely simulated dummy contents), atmospheric conditioning, and a sequence of rigorous simulated maneuvers—including clamp squeeze tests, push/pull slip-sheet dragging, and forklift drop-flat-on-base shocks from 20 cm heights—to ensure that unit loads do not shift, collapse, or suffer structural failure during transit.
